Coverage context

Submission completeness

The regional dashboard includes 1,727 of 1,740 schools. Three divisions reported 100% school submission.

Coverage note: High submission supports broad regional description, but the results do not represent the 13 schools without submissions.
Substantial comparative inference

What the division results show

The following statements are descriptive inferences from the published percentages and coverage totals. They identify patterns, contrasts, and planning considerations without attributing causation.

Descriptive · Non-causal
1

Regional readiness is lower in English

Grade Ready accounts for 29.87% in Filipino and 24.58% in English. The combined 3- and 2-levels-down shares are therefore 70.14% and 75.42%, respectively. Relative to Filipino, English has 4.06 percentage points more learners at 3-Levels Down, 1.22 points more at 2-Levels Down, and 5.29 points fewer at Grade Ready.

2

Kidapawan City has the strongest supplied readiness profile

Kidapawan City records the highest Grade Ready shares in both Filipino (45.26%) and English (40.49%), while also recording the lowest 3-Levels Down shares (20.73% and 24.09%). Tacurong City ranks second in Grade Ready in both languages at 38.39% and 32.51%.

3

Sarangani has the largest concentration at the lowest reported level

Sarangani records the lowest Grade Ready shares in Filipino (22.87%) and English (16.97%) and the highest 3-Levels Down shares (33.97% and 40.77%). The Grade Ready spread between Kidapawan City and Sarangani is 22.39 percentage points in Filipino and 23.52 points in English.

4

Above- and below-regional patterns differ slightly by language

General Santos City, Kidapawan City, Koronadal City, and Tacurong City exceed the regional Grade Ready percentage in both languages. Sultan Kudarat is above the Filipino regional figure but 0.55 point below the English figure; South Cotabato is 0.50 point below the Filipino figure but 0.63 point above the English figure. Cotabato and Sarangani are below the regional Grade Ready percentages in both languages.

5

Every division shows a lower Grade Ready share in English

The English Grade Ready percentage is lower than the Filipino percentage in all eight divisions. The language gap ranges from 1.60 points in Koronadal City to 7.22 points in Sultan Kudarat. Seven divisions also have a higher 3-Levels Down share in English; Koronadal City is the exception, where that share is 2.25 points lower in English but the 2-Levels Down share is 3.85 points higher.

6

Percentages and assessment volume should be read together

Cotabato accounts for 70,875 learners, or 27.93% of the regional assessed population, followed by South Cotabato with 46,238 (18.22%). Together they represent 46.15% of assessed learners. Cotabato's Grade Ready shares are 28.50% in Filipino and 21.99% in English, so planning based only on rankings would understate the absolute scale of learners represented there.

7

The 2-Levels Down group is the largest regional category

At the regional level, 2-Levels Down is the largest category in Filipino (39.96%) and English (41.18%). It is also the largest Filipino category in six of eight divisions and the largest English category in seven of eight divisions. This identifies a broad intermediate support group alongside the learners requiring the most intensive support at 3-Levels Down.

8

Coverage is high but not perfectly complete

School submission is 99.25% region-wide. Kidapawan City, Koronadal City, and Tacurong City report 100% submission. Sultan Kudarat has the lowest rate at 98.58% (347 of 352 schools), followed by General Santos City at 98.68% and South Cotabato at 98.74%. The 13 missing school submissions should remain visible when interpreting small differences.

Interpretive boundary. These are aggregate, cross-sectional BoSY results for Grades 4–6. The supplied source does not provide grade-specific performance percentages, learner-level records, prior-year trends, or explanatory variables. The comparisons therefore do not establish instructional quality, school effectiveness, growth, or reasons for the observed differences. Any follow-up analysis should retain the same instrument, reporting definitions, cohort scope, and coverage rules.
